translation_en: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Sulayman narrated to me, from Sharik ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard Ibn Malik say: On the night the Messenger of Allah was taken on the Night Journey from the Mosque of the Ka‘bah, three men came to him before revelation had come to him, while he was asleep in the Sacred Mosque. The first said, “Which of them is he?” The middle one said, “He is the best of them.” The last said, “Take the best of them.” That was that night. He did not see them again until they came to him another night, as his heart perceived them; his eyes slept but his heart did not sleep. Such is the case with the Prophets: their eyes sleep, but their hearts do not sleep. They did not speak to him until they carried him and placed him beside the well of Zamzam. Gabriel took charge of him. Gabriel split open the area from the base of his neck to his chest until he had opened his chest and abdomen. He washed them with Zamzam water using his hand until he had cleansed his interior. Then a gold basin was brought, containing a gold vessel filled with faith and wisdom. He filled his chest and the veins of his throat with it—meaning the veins of his throat—then closed it up. He ascended with him to the lowest heaven and knocked at one of its gates. The inhabitants of heaven called to him, “Who is this?” He said, “Gabriel.” They said, “Who is with you?” He said, “Muhammad.” They said, “Has he been sent?” He said, “Yes.” They said, “Welcome to him.” The inhabitants of heaven rejoiced at him. The inhabitants of heaven do not know what Allah intends on earth until He informs them. In the lowest heaven he found Adam. Gabriel said to him, “This is your father; greet him.” He greeted him, and Adam returned the greeting and said, “Welcome, my son. What an excellent son you are.” In the lowest heaven there were two rivers flowing. He asked, “What are these two rivers, Gabriel?” He said, “These are the sources of the Nile and the Euphrates.” Then he proceeded through the heaven and came upon another river, above which was a palace of pearl and emerald. He struck his hand into it, and it was musk. He asked, “What is this, Gabriel?” He said, “This is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has kept for you.” Then he ascended to the second heaven. Its angels said to him what the angels of the first heaven had said: “Who is this?” He said, “Gabriel.” They said, “Who is with you?” He said, “Muhammad.” They said, “Has he been sent to him?” He said, “Yes.” They said, “Welcome to him.” Then he ascended with him to the third heaven, and they said what the first and second had said. Then he ascended with him to the fourth heaven, and they said the same. Then he ascended with him to the fifth heaven, and they said the same. Then he ascended with him to the sixth heaven, and they said the same. Then he ascended with him to the seventh heaven, and they said the same. In every heaven were Prophets whose names he mentioned. I remembered Idris in the second, Harun in the fourth, another in the fifth whose name I did not retain, Ibrahim in the sixth, and Musa in the seventh, because of the distinction of Allah’s speech to him. Musa said, “My Lord, I did not think anyone would be raised above me.” Then he ascended with him above that to a place known only to Allah, until he reached the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. The Compeller, Lord of Might, drew near and came close, until he was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. Allah revealed to him among what He revealed: “Fifty prayers for your community every day and night.” Then he descended until he reached Musa. Musa stopped him and asked, “O Muhammad, what did your Lord enjoin upon you?” He said, “He enjoined fifty prayers every day and night.” Musa said, “Your community cannot bear that. Go back, and ask your Lord to lighten it for you and them.” The Prophet turned toward Gabriel as though consulting him about it, and Gabriel indicated, “Yes, if you wish.” He took him up to the Compeller, and while he was in his place he said, “My Lord, lighten it for us, for my community cannot bear this.” He reduced ten prayers for him. Then he returned to Musa, who stopped him. Musa kept sending him back to his Lord until it became five prayers. Then Musa stopped him at the five and said, “O Muhammad, by Allah, I urged my people, the Children of Israel, to do less than this, but they were too weak and left it. Your community is weaker in bodies, hearts, physical strength, eyesight, and hearing, so go back and ask your Lord to lighten it for you.” Each time, the Prophet turned toward Gabriel for his advice, and Gabriel did not object. At the fifth time, he raised him and said, “My Lord, my community is weak in their bodies, hearts, hearing, and physical strength, so lighten it for us.” The Compeller said, “O Muhammad.” He replied, “At Your service and at Your pleasure.” He said, “The decree with Me is not changed. As I prescribed for you in the Mother of the Book, every good deed is multiplied tenfold. Thus it is fifty in the Mother of the Book, but five for you.” He returned to Musa, who asked, “What did you do?” He said, “He lightened it for us; He gives us ten times the reward for every good deed.” Musa said, “By Allah, I urged the Children of Israel to do less than that, but they left it. Go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it for you further.” The Messenger of Allah said, “Musa, by Allah, I am now too shy before my Lord, after repeatedly going back to Him.” He said, “Then descend in Allah’s name.” He said: He awoke while he was in the Sacred Mosque.
